data.name: Diwan
data.gender_notes: Diwan is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Diwan (ديوان) means a council or a gathering place, especially for scholars and religious leaders. It can also refer to a literary work or a collection of poetry. In the Islamic context, it symbolizes wisdom, knowledge, and community. The name Diwan carries the meaning “Council, gathering place” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Diwan usually hope their child will grow to embody council, gathering place and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A place of wisdom, knowledge, and community.
data.etymology: Diwan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Council, gathering place.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Diwan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: ديوان
in_arabic.meaning: ديوان هو مكان للنظر في الأمور الحكومية أو الشعرية
in_arabic.long_meaning: الديوان هو مكان للنظر في الأمور الحكومية أو الشعرية، و يعود أصل الكلمة إلى الفارسية وتعني مكانا للاجتماع أو القاعة، و في اللغة العربية، الديوان هو كتاب أو مجموعة من القصائد الشعرية، و يطلق أيضا على مكان الاجتماعات الرسمية أو الحكومية.

in_urdu.name: دیوان
in_urdu.meaning: دیوان کا مطلب ہے جہاں سرکاری یا شعری مسائل پر غور کیا جائے
in_urdu.long_meaning: دیوان فارسی سے ماخوذ ہے اور اس کا مطلب ہے ملاقات کا مقام یا ہال، عربی زبان میں دیوان کو شاعری کی کتاب یا مجموعہ کے طور پر جانا جاتا ہے، اور سرکاری یا رسمی اجلاسوں کے مقام کے طور پر بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے، اسلامی تقليد میں اس کا اہم کردار ہے.

in_hindi.name: दीवान
in_hindi.meaning: दीवान का अर्थ है जहां सरकारी या काव्यात्मक मामलों पर विचार किया जाता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: दीवान फारसी से लिया गया है और इसका अर्थ है मिलने का स्थान या हॉल, अरबी भाषा में दीवान को काव्य की पुस्तक या संग्रह के रूप में जाना जाता है, और सरकारी या औपचारिक बैठकों के स्थान के रूप में भी प्रयोग किया जाता है, इस्लामी परंपरा में इसकी महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका है.

in_pashto.name: ديوان
in_pashto.meaning: ديوان دى هغه ځاى چى د دولتي يا شعرى مسايلو په اړه پکې غور کيږي
in_pashto.long_meaning: ديوان د فارسي ژبې څخه اخيستل شوى دى او د دې مطلب دى چى د راغونډېدلو ځاى يا هال، په عربي ژبه کې ديوان د شعر کتاب يا ټولګه په توګه پيژندل کيږي، او د دولتي يا رسمي غونډو د ځاى په توګه هم کارول کيږي، په افغان او پښتني دود کې يې مهم رول دى.

in_english.name: Diwan
in_english.meaning: Diwan refers to a gathering place for government or poetic matters
in_english.long_meaning: The term Diwan originates from Persian, signifying a place of assembly or hall. In Arabic, it denotes a book of poetry or a collection. Historically, it has been used to describe a venue for official or governmental meetings. In Islamic tradition, Diwan holds cultural significance as a platform for administrative and literary activities.

data.cultural_impact: The name Diwan holds special significance in Islamic culture, as it represents a gathering place for scholars, poets, and spiritual leaders. The concept of Diwan is closely tied to the traditional Islamic educational institutions like madrasas and universities, which have been instrumental in preserving and disseminating Islamic knowledge. The name has also been used for various literary works in both Arabic and Persian languages, emphasizing the importance of knowledge and learning in Islamic tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: Diwan holds a special place in Islamic spirituality, as it signifies the assembly of the seekers of wisdom and knowledge. In Sufism, the Muslim mystical tradition, the concept of Diwan represents the divine gathering or assembly of spiritual seekers, guided by the wisdom of the spiritual master or Pir. The poems and verses in Sufi Diwans serve as a source of inspiration, knowledge, and guidance for the spiritual journey towards union with the Divine.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Khaldun's Muqaddimah, written around 1377-1382 AD. The name Diwan carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun described the Diwan as a financial and administrative institution, which was used by the Muslim rulers to manage their territories, collect taxes, and distribute resources. He noted that the Diwan was an essential element of the Islamic state, and its effective functioning was important for the stability and prosperity of the empire.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's Kitab al-Ittiqad fi Funun al-Islam, written around 1401-1402 AD. The name Diwan carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Maqrizi described the Diwan as a court office responsible for recording the ruler's decrees, managing the royal household, and supervising the collection and distribution of revenues. He noted that the Diwan was an important institution in the administration of the Islamic state, and its efficient functioning was essential for the effective governance of the empire.
